title: The Moomins and the Great Flood (Småtrollen och den stora översvämningen)

access.edition_or_version: First edition, 1945 (Finland-Swedish); first of the Moomin books

mechanics.premise: Moomintroll and Moominmamma search through a flooded landscape for Moominpappa, encountering dangers before finding a valley to settle.
mechanics.point_of_view: Third-person narration close to the small, curious protagonists, with a gentle comic tone.
mechanics.invented_world_and_props: A habitable, self-contained world of whimsical creatures whose adventures stay domestic in scale, so the invented feels liveable rather than grand.
mechanics.play_frame: The fantastic setting is treated as ordinary life, so strangeness is accepted rather than marvelled at or explained.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Gentle humour, soft irony, anthropomorphic invention, and a mixture of cosiness with real small-scale fear.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Displacement and mild fear -> companionship and resourcefulness -> warm arrival and settlement.
mechanics.dialogue: Affectionate, idiosyncratic family dialogue carrying much of the characterization and humour.
mechanics.conventions: A forerunner of the main Moomin series; combines the children's adventure with a philosophical, gently comic sensibility.
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Builds a distinctly Northern, habitable fantasy whose delights are social and domestic rather than heroic.
mechanics.critical_reception: Jansson's Moomin books became classics of Finnish literature and are praised for individualistic characters, complicated plots, and sophisticated humour.
mechanics.audience_reception: Global classic translated into dozens of languages, adapted to comics, television, film, and an opera.
